The '''2025 NCAA Division I FBS football season''' was the 156th season of [[college football]] in the United States, the 120th season organized by the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA), and the 50th of the highest level of competition, the [[NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision|Football Bowl Subdivision]] (FBS). The regular season began on August 23 and ended on December 13. The postseason began on December 13, and, aside from any all-star games that are scheduled, ended on January 19, 2026, with the [[2026 College Football Playoff National Championship|College Football Playoff National Championship]] at [[Hard Rock Stadium]] in [[Miami Gardens, Florida]].

The [[2025 Indiana Hoosiers football team|Indiana Hoosiers]] defeated the [[2025 Miami Hurricanes football team|Miami Hurricanes]] by a score of 27–21 to claim their first national championship in school history. The Hoosiers became the first FBS team since the [[1894 Yale Bulldogs football team|1894 Yale Bulldogs]] to have a perfect 16–0 season. This was the second season of the 12-team [[College Football Playoff]] (CFP) system.

==Rule changes==
The following playing rule changes were approved by the NCAA Playing Rules Oversight Committee on April 17, 2025:<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.ncaa.org/news/2025/4/16/media-center-changes-to-injury-timeouts-approved-in-football.aspx |title=Changes to Injury Timeouts Approved in Football |publisher=NCAA |date=April 16, 2025 |access-date=April 17, 2025}}</ref> 
* In an effort to reduce feigned injuries, if medical personnel have to enter the field to tend to an injured player after the ball is spotted by officials ready for play, that team will be charged a timeout (or a five-yard delay of game penalty if out of timeouts). If this occurs after the two-minute timeout (and the injury is the only reason for the clock to stop), a 10-second runoff applies if the team is out of timeouts.
* Starting with the third overtime period, teams will only be permitted one timeout to use until the game is concluded. Previously teams received a timeout for each overtime period, including the two-point attempts that begin with the third overtime.
* Eliminating media timeouts after the second overtime period, and reducing the mandatory rest periods in games without media timeouts to only after the second overtime period (instead of after the second and fourth overtimes).
* Once a decision is made on instant replay reviews, the referee will only use the terms "Overturned" and "Upheld". "Confirmed" or "Stands" will no longer be used.
* On punt formations, no player can be directly in line of the snap to a potential kicker and no player can be inside of the frame of the snapper to qualify as a legal scrimmage kick formation. If these requirements are not met, five players numbered 50–79 must be on the line of scrimmage. Also, if the snapper is on the end of a line, he loses the scrimmage kick protection and the defense can line up a player over the snapper.
* If a player on the kickoff return team gives a "T" signal with his arms, the team gives up their right to return the kickoff and the play will be whistled dead once the ball is caught or recovered.
* Enhanced rules regarding words or signals used to distract opponents trying to put the ball in play. The terms "stem" and "move" would only be permitted for defenses, and defenses cannot use cadence or sounds that simulate offensive team signals.
* Included players attempting to recover a loose ball to the list of "defenseless players".
* Contact to an offensive player in a passing posture is now considered "Roughing the Passer". If targeting occurs with this act, the roughing the passer penalty would remain even if the targeting penalty is overturned on replay.
* Added "simulating brandishing a weapon" to the list of acts considered unsportsmanlike conduct.
* Codifying the rule change from [[2024 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2024's Ohio State at Oregon game]], after the two-minute timeout, teams called for having 12 or more players participating in a down will be penalized five yards, and the offense would have the option to reset the game clock to the time at the start of the play. If the 12th or more player(s) were running off the field and had no influence on the play, the yardage penalty would apply but no clock reset option would be available. The clock reset option is also available without accepting the penalty.
* The Coach to Player (C2P green dot) communication technology currently used in FBS will be a permissible option for the Football Championship Subdivision (FCS). In 2026, the C2P technology will be allowed in Divisions II and III.

==Points of emphasis==

* Continued focus on protection of defenseless players, concussions, pre-snap actions from both offense/defense, and feigning injuries.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ncaapublications.com/p-4693-2025-ncaa-football-rules-book.aspx |title=2025 Official Football Rules |publisher=NCAA |date=June 19, 2025 |access-date=August 22, 2025}}</ref>
* Focus on penalizing taunting actions by players and pre-game actions between teams that become unsportsmanlike conduct.
* Sideline control, including leaving the playing area to dispute an officiating decision.
* Illegal contact against a passer.
* Pace of play and substituting during up-tempo offenses, ensuring defenses are not at a disadvantage before the snap.

== Headlines ==
* April 25, 2025 – The [[University of Kentucky]] (UK) board of trustees approved a proposal to transfer the [[Kentucky Wildcats|UK athletic program]] to a separate though related non-profit company known as Champions Blue, LLC. Both UK and outside media characterized the move, believed to be the first of its type by a major university, as a reaction to the then-impending settlement of the ''[[House v. NCAA]]'' legal case, which led to a formal revenue-sharing arrangement between athletic programs and student-athletes.<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://uknow.uky.edu/campus-news/new-model-represents-innovative-approach-future-college-athletics |title=New model represents innovative approach to future of college athletics |publisher=University of Kentucky |date=April 24, 2025 |access-date=April 27, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/kentucky-board-of-trustees-approves-shifting-universitys-athletics-department-into-limited-liability-company/ |title=Kentucky board of trustees approves shifting university's athletics department into limited liability company |first=Will |last=Backus |website=CBSSports.com |date=April 25, 2025 |access-date=April 27, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2025/04/24/university-of-kentucky-wildcats-ncaa-house-settlement-champions-blue-llc-lexington-ky/83247581007/ |title=University of Kentucky, ahead of House settlement, approves board to help navigate change |first=Payton |last=Titus |newspaper=[[Courier Journal]] |date=April 27, 2025 |access-date=April 27, 2025}}</ref>
* July 21 – The American Athletic Conference announced a name change to the [[American Conference (NCAA)|American Conference]] as part of a comprehensive rebranding strategy. The conference will also no longer use an initialism, opting for "American" as its short form.<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://theamerican.org/news/2025/7/20/about-american-conference-launches-modernized-brand-identity-ahead-of-football-media-days.aspx |title=American Conference Launches Modernized Brand Identity Ahead of Football Media Days |publisher=American Conference |date=July 21, 2025 |access-date=July 21, 2025}}</ref>
* September 4 – The NCAA FBS Oversight Committee voted on major changes to the [[NCAA transfer portal|transfer portal]]. Under the proposal, the current 30-day period for players to enter the portal, divided into a 20-day December window and a 10-day April window, would be replaced by a single 10-day window that would run from January 2–11. This new 10-day window would apply to both undergraduate and graduate transfers. The committee also recommended that the month of December become a [[College recruiting|recruiting]] "dead period" during which coaches and recruits cannot meet in person, and that the signing date for new recruits change from August 1 to November 15 of a recruit's senior year in high school.<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.ncaa.org/news/2025/9/4/media-center-fbs-oversight-committee-proposes-changes-to-notification-of-transfer-window.aspx |title=FBS Oversight Committee proposes changes to notification-of-transfer window |publisher=NCAA |date=September 4, 2025 |access-date=September 5, 2025}}</ref>
* September 17 – The NCAA Division I Administrative Committee approved the proposed single January transfer portal, but chose not to adopt the proposed January 2–11 dates. In response to feedback from FBS and FCS players, the oversight committees for both subdivisions were to discuss the dates and duration of the portal, with the Administrative Committee to set the final parameters at its scheduled October meeting. Players still competing in postseason play when the new portal closes will have a 5-day portal after their teams' final games, and the existing 30-day window for players undergoing a head coaching change will tentatively remain in place.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/46296718/ncaa-eliminates-spring-transfer-portal-window-football |title=NCAA eliminates spring transfer portal window for football |first=Max |last=Olson |website=ESPN.com |date=September 17, 2025 |access-date=September 18, 2025}}</ref>
* September 29 – The FBS Oversight Committee recommended that the single January transfer portal be open for 15 days from January 2–16 instead of the originally proposed 10-day window. The revised recommendation also creates a 5-day window for players involved in postseason contests on or after January 12, with the window opening on the day after the team's last game. The Administrative Committee, whose next meeting was October 7–8, had to approve these changes before they took effect. The committee also discussed possible changes to the 30-day window for players undergoing a head coaching change, with continuing discussions set for its next scheduled meeting.<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.ncaa.org/news/2025/9/29/media-center-di-fbs-oversight-committee-modifies-notification-of-transfer-period-recommendation.aspx |title=DI FBS Oversight Committee modifies notification-of-transfer period recommendation |publisher=NCAA |date=September 29, 2025 |access-date=October 2, 2025}}</ref>
* October 8:
** The Administrative Committee, which officially renamed itself the Division I Cabinet at its scheduled meeting, introduced a proposal to expand allowed logos on student-athletes' uniforms and equipment beyond those of the manufacturer. It also approved the following changes to the transfer portal, effective immediately:<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.ncaa.org/news/2025/10/8/media-center-di-administrative-committee-introduces-proposal-for-commercial-logos-on-uniforms-apparel-and-equipment.aspx |title=DI Administrative Committee introduces proposal for commercial logos on uniforms, apparel and equipment |publisher=NCAA |date=October 9, 2025 |access-date=October 9, 2025}}</ref>
*** The committee approved the previously recommended single window running from January 2–16. This only affects entry into the portal.
*** The window for players undergoing a head coaching change was modified. The window for these players will open five calendar days after the hiring or public announcement of a new head coach, and run for 15 days. Should a school not hire or announce a new head coach after 30 days from the previous coach's departure, a separate 15-day window will open on the 31st day, provided that the 31st day is on or after January 3. The opportunity for such a window will exist through June 30.
* October 12 – [[James Franklin (American football coach)|James Franklin]] was fired at [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State]] after 12 seasons with the school. Franklin's contract had called for a buyout of more than $49 million, at the time the second biggest buyout in college football history, but a much lower buyout of $9 million was later negotiated when Franklin was hired for the vacancy at [[Virginia Tech Hokies football|Virginia Tech]].<ref name=Marcello>{{cite news |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/james-franklin-buyout-reduced-penn-state-virginia-tech/ |title=Penn State, James Franklin agree to drastically reduced buyout as ex-coach moves on to Virginia Tech |first=Brandon |last=Marcello |website=CBSSports.com |date=November 17, 2025 |access-date=November 20, 2025}}</ref> Franklin was 4–21 against AP top-10 opponents in his time at Penn State. Associate head coach [[Terry Smith (American football, born 1969)|Terry Smith]] served as the Nittany Lions' interim head coach for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Penn State AD: James Franklin's Firing Went Far Beyond Recent Struggles |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/college-football/penn-state-ad-james-franklins-firing-went-far-beyond-recent-struggles |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=www.foxsports.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-10-12 |title=Penn State fires Franklin amid midseason free fall |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/46573030/penn-state-fires-head-coach-james-franklin-sources-say |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>
* December 10 – [[Sherrone Moore]] was fired for cause by [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan]] after 2 seasons as the head coach, due to evidence he allegedly engaged in an inapproriate relationship with a staff member.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-12-10 |title=U-M fires Moore for inappropriate relationship |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/47269785/sources-michigan-fires-coach-sherrone-moore-9-3-season |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |first1=Pete |last1=Thamel |first2=Dan |last2=Wetzel |first3=Adam |last3=Schefter |author-link3=Adam Schefter |author-link2=Dan Wetzel |author-link1=Pete Thamel}}</ref> Immediately following his firing, Moore spiralled out of control, went to the house of the staff member he was alleged to have an affair with, and threatened to take both her life and his own life.<ref>{{cite news |last=McMann |first=Aaron |date=December 10, 2025 |title=Fired Michigan coach Sherrone Moore jailed amid assault probe |url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2025/12/fired-michigan-coach-sherrone-moore-jailed-after-alleged-assault-police-say.html |accessdate=December 10, 2025 |website=[[MLive.com]]}}</ref> He was soon arrested and charged for three crimes: felonious third-degree home invasion, stalking in a domestic relationship, and breaking and entering.<ref>{{cite news |date=December 12, 2025 |title=Fired Michigan coach Sherrone Moore charged with three crimes |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/47286996/fired-michigan-coach-sherrone-moore-charged-three-crimes |accessdate=December 12, 2025 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

===Bowl games===

Normally, a team is required to have a .500 minimum [[winning percentage]] during the regular season to become [[bowl-eligible]] (six wins for an 11- or 12-game schedule, and seven wins for a 13-game schedule). If there are not enough winning teams to fulfill all open bowl slots, teams with losing records may be chosen to fill available bowl slots. Additionally, on the rare occasion in which a conference champion does not meet eligibility requirements, they are usually still chosen for bowl games via [[Bids to college bowl games|tie-ins]] for their conference.

==Television changes==
This is the first season of a new television contract for the [[Big 12 Conference]] with [[ESPN College Football|ESPN]], [[Fox College Football|Fox Sports]] and [[College Football on TNT Sports|TNT Sports]]. ESPN holds the rights to the top four college football games per season, and twelve of the top twenty games, along with the [[Big 12 Championship Game]] on [[College Football on ABC|ABC]]. TNT Sports sublicenses thirteen games from ESPN.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Thamel|first=Pete|title=Big 12 nears six-year, $2.28B TV extension deal with ESPN, Fox|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/34910144/big-12-nears-six-year-228b-tv-extension-deal-espn-fox|website=ESPN.com|date=October 30, 2022|access-date=March 5, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Axelrod|first=Ben|title=TNT lands Big 12 games from ESPN as part of WBD-NBA settlement|url=https://awfulannouncing.com/tnt-sports/lands-big-12-games-wbd-nba-settlement.html|work=Awful Announcing|date=November 18, 2024|access-date=March 5, 2025}}</ref>

The [[Pac-12 Conference]] renewed their media partnership with [[CW Football Saturday|The CW]] for the 2025 season, while also agreeing to two-game deals with ESPN and [[College Football on CBS Sports|CBS Sports]]. While The CW will continue to carry majority of the home games for [[Oregon State Beavers football|Oregon State]] and [[Washington State Cougars football|Washington State]], ESPN will carry two Oregon State home games and CBS will carry one home game from each school in primetime.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 29, 2025 |title=2025 Pac-12 football to be featured nationally across CBS, The CW and ESPN |url=https://pac-12.com/news/2025/4/23/2025-pac-12-football-to-be-featured-nationally-across-cbs-the-cw-and-espn.aspx |access-date=April 29, 2025 |work=Pac-12 Conference}}</ref>

This is the final year of the [[Mountain West Conference]]'s broadcast agreement with [[Fox College Football|Fox Sports]] and CBS Sports. The conference has not yet announced a new agreement.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Murray|first=Chris|title=Mountain West announces media rights deal with CBS, Fox. Here are the details.|url=https://nevadasportsnet.com/news/reporters/mountain-west-announces-media-rights-deal-with-cbs-fox-here-are-the-details|work=Nevada Sports Net|date=January 9, 2020|access-date=April 30, 2025}}</ref> Despite being announced as a multi-year deal, the Mountain West did not continue an agreement with TNT Sports from 2024 to air 14 games on [[TruTV]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Huddleston|first=Ben|date=May 30, 2025 |title=News: March Madness, softball, CW, and more |url=https://www.sportsmediawatch.com/2025/05/march-madness-expansion-mlb-softball-investment-cw-bowl-games/ |access-date=May 31, 2025 |work=Sports Media Watch}}</ref>
